newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to verify ownership of Jewish gold.
newsitem.headline: Italy to verify ownership of Jewish gold.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Tuesday it had set up a commission to assess who owns a stash of gold, jewellery and other valuables apparently stripped from Jews at a Nazi death camp that have turned up in an official vault.
It said in a statement that the commission would have two months to carry out its investigations.
The Treasury said it would also be looking into how the five crates of World War Two personal treasures had come to be deposited with the Treasury for safekeeping.
"The inspection of the contents will be carried out in the oresence of representatives of the Jewish community," the statement said.
Newspapers on Sunday said the valuables had been traced to the vault by the prefect, or central government representative, in the northeast city of Trieste, Michele De Feis.
The Treasury confirmed that the articles had come from the provincial treasury office in Trieste. The city was under Nazi occupation from September 1943 until the end of the war in 1945.
De Feis launched an inquiry last year into the whereabouts of the missing treasure after Trieste's Jewish community raised a claim for compensation for victims of the Holocaust.
Many of the city's Jews perished at the nearby Risiera di San Sabba, the only German Nazi death camp in Italy.
La Repubblica newspaper said the plundered treasure was moved to Klagenfurt in Austria by the retreating Germans in 1945 and returned to Trieste in the early 1950s.

Newspapers said Trieste's Jewish community raised the case after publicity about the controversy over whether Swiss banks kept millions of dollars deposited in secret accounts by Jews before and during the Second World War.
